market.title: Men's US Open Winner - 2026
resolutionNote: Resolves Yes for whichever player wins the 2026 US Open Men's Singles title - only the five most-backed contenders are tracked on this page, out of 35+ players still listed on Kalshi and 49+ on Polymarket.

Kalshi's own wording (per player): "If [Player] wins the 2026 US Open Men's Singles professional tennis tournament, then the market resolves to Yes." A player who withdraws or is otherwise eliminated from contention resolves No immediately, without waiting for the tournament to finish.

Both of the tournament's top seeds are already out and resolved No: Jannik Sinner withdrew before his opening match with a knee injury, and Novak Djokovic lost in the first round to Mariano Navone - the first time he's ever lost that early at the US Open.
One real gap between the platforms: Polymarket's cutoff is Sep 13, 2026, while Kalshi's runs a little later, expected around Sep 14, 2026 once the final concludes.

text: The competition has seen drama from the first round, firstly in the premature exit of Novak Djokovic after a shock early defeat and secondly in the withdrawal of world No.1 Jannik Sinner with a knee injury.
Many believe this has left the door open for Carlos Alcaraz even though a wrist injury has forced him off of the courts for the past five months.

Alcaraz put any doubt to bed though after defeating Roman Safiullin 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 in his first game back, with former US Open Champ Andy Roddick even commenting that Alcaraz's forehand speed seemed higher than last year.
Alexander Zverev is now the tournament's top remaining seed but remains second to Alcaraz in the odds at around 21%, while Ben Shelton and Taylor Fritz trail behind.
The final is scheduled for Sunday, September 13.
Alcaraz's straight-sets win over Safiullin has pushed him further clear at 37%, with Zverev now second at 20% after a scare against Lorenzo Sonego.
